title: From DNA Fragment to Verified Clone

scenes.tts: A colony has survived an antibiotic. Does it carry the DNA you wanted? Survival is encouraging, but it answers only one question. Follow one candidate insert through a chain that narrows what the colony might contain.
scenes.caption: A colony has survived an antibiotic. Does it carry the DNA you wanted? Survival is encouraging, but it answers only one question. Follow one candidate insert through a chain that narrows what the colony might contain.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP for both films: original DNA and outlines grey; insert and primers yellow; plasmids and new copies blue; supported results green; unresolved or failed results red. A large grey bacterium fills the frame. One green colony grows above it while a yellow insert-shaped gap remains a red question mark inside a blue plasmid. The colony slowly expands as the question mark pulses.
scenes.narration: A colony has survived an antibiotic. Does it carry the DNA you wanted? Survival is encouraging, but it answers only one question. Follow one candidate insert through a chain that narrows what the colony might contain.

scenes.visual: Transform the colony and question mark into the title, 'From DNA Fragment to Verified Clone'. Keep a small blue plasmid rotating behind the words.

scenes.tts: Start with a blue plasmid and a yellow DNA insert. Matching restriction cuts create compatible ends on both pieces. Their exposed bases can pair. DNA ligase seals the backbone. This creates a recombinant candidate, but other products can form too. Compatibility permits a join; it does not verify the joined pieces.
scenes.caption: Start with a blue plasmid and a yellow DNA insert. Matching restriction cuts create compatible ends on both pieces. Their exposed bases can pair. DNA ligase seals the backbone. This creates a recombinant candidate, but other products can form too. Compatibility permits a join; it does not verify the joined pieces.
scenes.visual: A large blue plasmid opens at one labelled restriction site. A yellow insert slides between its compatible block-shaped ends. The ends pair, then blue ligase badges travel around both junctions and close two visible backbone gaps. Beside the candidate, a smaller empty blue plasmid quietly closes to show another possible product.
scenes.narration: Start with a blue plasmid and a yellow DNA insert. Matching restriction cuts create compatible ends on both pieces. Their exposed bases can pair. DNA ligase seals the backbone. This creates a recombinant candidate, but other products can form too. Compatibility permits a join; it does not verify the joined pieces.

scenes.tts: The plasmid carries an origin, a selectable marker, and a cloning site. The origin lets the host copy the circle. The marker can let plasmid-bearing cells survive an antibiotic. The cloning site holds the insert. These parts make propagation possible, but none reads the insert's complete sequence.
scenes.caption: The plasmid carries an origin, a selectable marker, and a cloning site. The origin lets the host copy the circle. The marker can let plasmid-bearing cells survive an antibiotic. The cloning site holds the insert. These parts make propagation possible, but none reads the insert's complete sequence.
scenes.visual: Carry the same plasmid forward and enlarge it. Three labelled blocks orbit into fixed positions: 'origin', 'selectable marker', and 'cloning site'. The origin block emits two daughter plasmids. The marker raises a green shield. The yellow insert locks into the cloning site, while its internal bases remain covered by a red question mark.
scenes.narration: The plasmid carries an origin, a selectable marker, and a cloning site. The origin lets the host copy the circle. The marker can let plasmid-bearing cells survive an antibiotic. The cloning site holds the insert. These parts make propagation possible, but none reads the insert's complete sequence.

scenes.tts: Next, the plasmid enters bacteria by transformation. Only some cells take up a circle. Those cells divide, copying the plasmid as they grow. Cells with no plasmid remain mixed among them. The tube now contains several possibilities, so the experiment needs a way to narrow the population.
scenes.caption: Next, the plasmid enters bacteria by transformation. Only some cells take up a circle. Those cells divide, copying the plasmid as they grow. Cells with no plasmid remain mixed among them. The tube now contains several possibilities, so the experiment needs a way to narrow the population.
scenes.visual: The candidate plasmid moves into one of several large grey bacterial cartoons. That cell divides twice, with a blue circle passing into each daughter. Other grey cells remain plasmid-free. All cells drift toward a wide plate, keeping plasmid-bearing and plasmid-free cells visibly mixed.
scenes.narration: Next, the plasmid enters bacteria by transformation. Only some cells take up a circle. Those cells divide, copying the plasmid as they grow. Cells with no plasmid remain mixed among them. The tube now contains several possibilities, so the experiment needs a way to narrow the population.

scenes.tts: Selection asks whether a cell probably carries a plasmid with the marker. Spread the cells on antibiotic. Plasmid-free cells stop growing. Marker-bearing cells form colonies. Yet an empty vector can carry the same marker. Survival enriches plasmid-bearing cells; it does not identify the construct inside each colony.
scenes.caption: Selection asks whether a cell probably carries a plasmid with the marker. Spread the cells on antibiotic. Plasmid-free cells stop growing. Marker-bearing cells form colonies. Yet an empty vector can carry the same marker. Survival enriches plasmid-bearing cells; it does not identify the construct inside each colony.
scenes.visual: Cells land across a plate labelled 'antibiotic'. Plasmid-free grey cells fade without any death symbol. Blue-plasmid cells expand into green colonies. One colony contains the yellow insert; another contains the small empty vector. Both remain equally green while red question marks hover above them.
scenes.narration: Selection asks whether a cell probably carries a plasmid with the marker. Spread the cells on antibiotic. Plasmid-free cells stop growing. Marker-bearing cells form colonies. Yet an empty vector can carry the same marker. Survival enriches plasmid-bearing cells; it does not identify the construct inside each colony.

scenes.tts: Several colonies remain, and their plasmids are hidden. Which next observation would separate an empty vector from the intended construct? Hold the plate in mind. You need evidence about the DNA inside a colony, not another test of antibiotic survival.
scenes.caption: Several colonies remain, and their plasmids are hidden. Which next observation would separate an empty vector from the intended construct? Hold the plate in mind. You need evidence about the DNA inside a colony, not another test of antibiotic survival.
scenes.visual: Zoom to two equal green colonies. Above them, show a choice fork with 'antibiotic again' on a blue shield and 'inspect plasmid DNA' on a closed grey panel. Do not highlight either choice. Red question marks drift slowly between the colonies and the fork.
scenes.narration: Several colonies remain, and their plasmids are hidden. Which next observation would separate an empty vector from the intended construct? Hold the plate in mind. You need evidence about the DNA inside a colony, not another test of antibiotic survival.

scenes.visual: Keep the two colonies and choice fork on screen. The outlines breathe gently and the question marks pulse once each second. Reveal no answer.

scenes.tts: Screening inspects the candidate DNA. A colony PCR or restriction digest can test whether fragments have expected sizes. A matching pattern moves a colony forward, but size is not sequence. Screening changes the odds. It does not turn a candidate into proof.
scenes.caption: Screening inspects the candidate DNA. A colony PCR or restriction digest can test whether fragments have expected sizes. A matching pattern moves a colony forward, but size is not sequence. Screening changes the odds. It does not turn a candidate into proof.
scenes.visual: Open the 'inspect plasmid DNA' panel. Samples from each colony travel into a schematic gel with a size ladder. One lane gains green bands at labelled expected positions; the other gains a red mismatched band. Mark the whole gel 'schematic'. The green candidate advances, still carrying a small red question mark.
scenes.narration: Screening inspects the candidate DNA. A colony PCR or restriction digest can test whether fragments have expected sizes. A matching pattern moves a colony forward, but size is not sequence. Screening changes the odds. It does not turn a candidate into proof.

scenes.tts: Sequence both junctions and the insert to test the bases and orientation. A correct sequence supports the intended construct. Expression is a separate question: the plasmid also needs a working promoter and other expression parts. Each result earns only the conclusion its measurement can support.
scenes.caption: Sequence both junctions and the insert to test the bases and orientation. A correct sequence supports the intended construct. scenes.visual: The green candidate plasmid unrolls into a labelled linear map. A scanner travels across 'left junction', 'insert', and 'right junction', turning each block green. Then a separate grey 'expression?' lamp appears beside a promoter-shaped block and remains unresolved.
scenes.narration: Sequence both junctions and the insert to test the bases and orientation. A correct sequence supports the intended construct. Expression is a separate question: the plasmid also needs a working promoter and other expression parts. Each result earns only the conclusion its measurement can support.

scenes.tts: The chain now makes sense. Compatible ends create possibilities. Transformation and growth create copies. Selection removes many cells without plasmids. Screening narrows the candidates. Sequencing tests the construct itself. Cloning succeeds by combining amplification with evidence, one inference at a time.

scenes.visual: Rebuild the entire carried chain as one continuous left-to-right path: compatible ends, growing bacteria, selective plate, schematic gel, sequence map. A green evidence line advances through each stage while red uncertainty shrinks. End with the verified plasmid large at centre, gently rotating.
scenes.narration: The chain now makes sense. Compatible ends create possibilities. Transformation and growth create copies. Selection removes many cells without plasmids. Screening narrows the candidates. Sequencing tests the construct itself. Cloning succeeds by combining amplification with evidence, one inference at a time.

scenes.visual: Clear everything to a dark field. Show one line only: 'Selection finds plasmids; screening narrows candidates; sequencing identifies the construct.'
